title: TransferTraj: A Vehicle Trajectory Learning Model for Region and Task Trans

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract claims 'an average improvement of 83.70% and 33.68% in zero-shot region transferability,' implying both figures refer to zero-shot transfer. However, Section 5.1 explicitly states: 'on the TP task, our method achieves improvements of 83.70% and 33.68% over SOTA models in zero-shot and few-shot settings.' The 33.68% figure corresponds to few-shot, not zero-shot transfer. This misrepresents the experimental setting.

The text claims 83.70% average improvement over SOTA for zero-shot TP. Calculating the average RMSE improvement of TransferTraj over START (wo ft) across the six transfer pairs in Table 4 yields approximately 83.9% (C→X: 82.57%, C→P: 85.01%, X→P: 82.71%, X→C: 87.89%, P→C: 85.64%, P→X: 79.79%; mean = 83.94%). Using MAE yields approximately 84.1%. Neither matches the claimed 83.70% exactly, and the computation method is unspecified.

The paper claims 'average 20.18%, 17.87%, and 7.94% gains over the SOTA baselines START, MM-STGED, and DOT on three tasks' for TransferTraj (wo ft). For TP, the RMSE improvement of TransferTraj (wo ft) over START averaged across three datasets is 24.80% (Chengdu: 33.01%, Xian: 25.34%, Porto: 16.06%), not 20.18%. For OD TTE, RMSE improvement over DOT averages 6.73%, not 7.94%. For TR, no straightforward averaging across datasets and sampling intervals reproduces 17.87%. The reported percentages are not verifiable from the data provided.

The text states 'our ablation study on SC-MoE demonstrates a substantial performance drop of 14.52% on the OD TTE task.' From Table 6, TransferTraj OD TTE RMSE = 2.861 and wo SC-MoE RMSE = 3.240. The percentage increase is (3.240−2.861)/2.861 = 13.25%, and the percentage decrease is (3.240−2.861)/3.240 = 11.70%. Neither equals 14.52%. Checking other metrics: MAE gives 25.49%, MAPE gives 23.76%. The value 14.52% cannot be reproduced from any metric in Table 6 for the OD TTE task columns.

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 1 (TP Task) vs Table 6 (Ablation study), TransferTraj row
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: In Table 1 (TP task, Chengdu), TransferTraj reports RMSE = 187.91 ± 8.65 and MAE = 144.53 ± 5.25. In Table 6 (ablation study), TransferTraj reports RMSE = 197.91 and MAE = 144.53. The MAE values are identical to two decimal places (144.53), but the RMSE values differ by 10.0. While the ablation table does not label the dataset/task explicitly, the context suggests it is the Chengdu TP task. Identical MAE with differing RMSE is statistically improbable and suggests a copying error or inconsistent experiment runs being reported as the same configuration.

Table 7 shows nine columns with headers 'Chengdu | Chengdu | Chengdu | Xi'an | Xi'an | Xi'an | Porto | Porto | Porto' but provides no sub-column labels indicating what each triplet of values represents. The caption mentions 'size of the learning model and the time required for training and testing,' but the table itself does not specify which column corresponds to model size, training time, or testing time, and gives no units for any measurement. This makes the table effectively uninterpretable without guessing.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 5.1 (Region transferability paragraph) and Table 5, Table 15
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper claims 'for the OD TTE task, the gains are 10.88% and 13.07% in zero-shot and few-shot settings.' For zero-shot OD TTE (Table 5), the RMSE improvement of TransferTraj over DOT averages 10.39% across six transfer pairs, MAE averages 11.18%, MAPE averages 11.09%. For few-shot OD TTE (Table 15), RMSE averages 9.28%, MAE averages 15.12%, MAPE averages 14.81%. None of these computed averages matches 10.88% or 13.07%. The paper does not specify which metric or averaging method yields these figures.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 5 (Experiments, OD TTE task description) and Section 4.2
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: For OD TTE, the paper specifies the input as '⟨p1, p′n⟩' with only the origin and destination points (the destination having masked temporal modality). However, the pre-training scheme in Section 4.2 always uses full-length trajectories with only some segments/points masked, never reducing the sequence to just two points. During pre-training, the model learns to attend over sequences of variable but substantial length. Inference with only two points represents an out-of-distribution sequence length that may not be supported by the model's positional encoding scheme (TRIE uses spatial-coordinate-based rotations that still function with two points, but the Transformer's behavior on drastically shorter sequences than those seen in pre-training is not validated or discussed).
